account:
Today I followed my appointments, including market business, an accounts review, and tea with my neighbour in the riverside quarter. The accounts review remains unresolved: the secretary found no financial records on the four great hall tables and does not know who holds the ledger. I do not know either. A written request is reportedly filed in the appointments chest. I checked the treasury and found 128 emeralds, which I left untouched; I have no evidence of missing money.

At tea, my neighbour mentioned vague talk of lights or some change near the bridge or port. She had no concrete details. The secretary says no plans or requests for work there have reached the office. I cannot yet tell whether there is actual work, ordinary activity, or merely a rumour, much less its purpose.

The innkeeper made a notably insistent request for my presence precisely at eighteen tomorrow in the great hall, with the secretary to remind and escort me. He described it only as a community hospitality matter and said to bring myself with no preparation. It may be a social gathering, but I have not been told the details and should not assume more. I confirmed attendance.

There has also been confusion over recording that meeting. The original appointment book is signed, so the secretary requested an emerald for a new writable book. I handed over one emerald, reducing my personal purse from thirty to twenty-nine, and requested that existing appointments be copied and both books retained. The secretary subsequently asked for the emerald again. My latest explanation was not heard because nobody was close enough. This looks like a communication or bookkeeping misunderstanding, not evidence of wrongdoing. I have not confirmed that the updated book has been completed. It is now just past nineteen, my scheduled time to return home.
